preamble: Place assimilation and fortition of the coda tap [ɾ] to the voiced velar stop [g] before a velar stop. In western Cuban Spanish (the provinces from Pinar del Río to Matanzas and Cienfuegos, including Havana, plus the municipalities of Corralillo and Trinidad), coda /ɾ/ and coda /l/ merge and assimilate to the next consonant; before /g/ and /k/ they surface as an unreleased [g˺], a geminate in larga la[g˺g]a and a voiced-voiceless sequence in barco ba[g˺k]o. Purga and pulga are both pu[g˺g]a. The unassimilated pronunciations remain more common. Before /k/ the descriptions differ: Lamb (1968) and Goodgall de Pruna (1970) report a voiceless onset [kk], while Guitart (1978, 2004), the acoustic study of Ruiz Hernández and Miyares Bermúdez (1984) and Carlson (2017) give a voiced first element (all as summarized by Arias 2019).
phoneticEffects: Regressive Assimilation, Place Assimilation, Fortition, Gemination

examples.note: [g˺] is an unreleased voiced velar stop.
Homophonous with pulga, because coda /l/ assimilates in the same way (Arias 2019); Wikipedia (Caribbean Spanish) gives pulga/purga [ˈpuɡːa], citing Guitart (1997).
Before voiceless /k/ the assimilated tap stays voiced in Arias's description; volcar gives vo[g˺k]ar from coda /l/.
Across a word boundary; Arias glosses the form as 'ideal garantía o idear garantía'.
